title: Nullable year undermines the replacement uniqueness constraint
reasoning: This migration removes the existing unique constraint on fast name/church, adds year as nullable, then replaces the constraint with uniqueness across name/church/year. On common Django-supported SQL backends, unique constraints do not treat NULL values as equal, so multiple Fast rows with the same name and church can coexist while year is NULL. Because the new field is added with blank=True/null=True and no backfill/default, all existing rows initially have NULL year, and future rows may also leave it NULL. That creates a data integrity hole compared with the removed unique_name_church constraint.
recommendation: Backfill year for existing Fast rows before adding the new constraint and make the field non-null if uniqueness must always include year, or use a conditional/expression constraint that preserves uniqueness for NULL years.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this migration group, and migration tests would need to assert duplicate Fast rows with NULL year are rejected after 0016.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a migration test that migrates through 0016 and attempts to create two Fast records with identical name/church and NULL year, expecting an IntegrityError or an explicit non-null validation path.
minimumFixScope: Update migration 0016 to backfill year and enforce non-null, or add an additional uniqueness constraint for rows where year is NULL.
